newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia aims at an average six pct growth rate.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia aims at an average six pct growth rate.

text.p: Tunisia, banking on dividends from its increasing integration into the world economy, said on Tuesday it aimed to average six percent real growth between 1997 and 2001, compared with 4.6 percent for the last five years.

"The new (development) plan for 1997-2001 aims at reaching a growth rate of six percent per year, in constant prices," Prime Minister Hamed Karoui told a meeting of international donors gathered to discuss financing the country's 9th development plan.

The final draft of the plan adopted by the cabinet last week and obtained by Reuters says this goal could be reached through an improvement of overall productivity of inputs expected to contribute 40 percent to the growth rate forecast.
It says that the goal requires intensified capital investment, the improvement of infrastructure and the reinforcement of the economy's competitiveness.
The six percent average rate implies a seven percent growth rate in manufacturing and the services sector and 4.3 percent expansion in agriculture.

Banking on the opening up of the economy to the world's economy, the plan forecasts an average annual growth rate of six percent at constant prices for exports of goods and servives, and of 5.9 percent for imports.

Export growth is based on expanding Tunisia's share of existing external markets and exporting to new markets within the European Union with which it signed a free trade zone accord in 1995, and elsewhere.

The plan puts investment at 5.38 billion dinars ($4.9 billion) in the agricuture and fishing sector, 4.80 billion dinars in manufacturing, of which 1.28 billion dinars will go to textiles and leather, and 4.05 billion for non-manufacturing industries.

Investments in services were put at 15.14 billion dinars, of which 4.70 billion dinars will go to transport and 1.69 billion dinars to telecommunications. In addition, 4.39 billion dinars are to be invested in social infrastructure, of which 1.07 billion dinars will be in education and training.

Total investment was put at 33.775 billion dinars, compared with 20.802 billion dinars during the last five years. Overall financing requirements for the development plan 1997-2001 are estimated at 42 billion dinars, of which 11.2 billion dinars will come from external funding.

The document forecasts average inflation at 3.7 percent a year for the period 1997-2001, compared with 4.8 percent a year during the last five years and 3.8 percent in 1996. Inflation is seen at 3.5 percent by the year 2001.
The country's external debt is expected to reach 12.58 billion dinars or 40.9 percent of GDP in 2001, compared to 9.62 billion dinars or 51.1 percent of GDP in 1996.
Debt servicing rate as a percentage of current revenue is expected to fall to 16.2 percent by the year 2001 compared to 17.7 percent at end of 1996.

Government's budget deficit to GDP is put an average rate of 2.6 percent yearly in 1997-2001 compared to 3.5 percent in 1992-1996. It is expected to reach 2.0 percent at end of 2001 compared to 3.9 percent at end of 1996. ($=1.1 dinar)
